t: the signs are positive commandments. These commandments are not instructions to perform a particular act, but commandments that teach about the very law of distinguishing.
splits the hoof. That the hoof is divided in two.
brings up the cud. A digestive process in which food passes from the mouth to the stomach and returns to the mouth, is chewed, and goes back to the stomach.
in the upper jaw. At the front of the upper jaw, referring to pure animals (Maggid Mishneh).
and every animal... except the camel. And likewise the hare and the hyrax, which are a type of wild animal.
with cut-off hooves. Whose hooves were removed, so that it cannot be checked whether it has split hooves.
that he recognize a camel. And know that the animal he found is not a camel.
whose mouth is cut. And one cannot check by its teeth whether it chews the cud.
cloven. Divided in two.
that he recognize a pig. And identify that this is not a pig.
at the sides of the tailbone. At the end of the spine, in the upper part of the thigh.
runs warp and weft. That there are two layers of flesh there whose fibers face different directions from each other.
arod. A wild donkey, which is impure.
in the form of an impure animal. An offspring in the likeness of an impure animal.
if it gave birth in front of him. That he himself saw that the one resembling an impure animal was born from the pure one.
in the form of a pig trailing after it. An offspring resembling a pig, behaving as though she were its mother.
for what grows from an impure animal is impure, and what grows from a pure one is pure. See also below 3:1.
therefore an impure fish etc. We assume it did not grow in its innards but was swallowed by it.
in the innards of. Inside its body.
two backs and two spines. A defect resembling conjoined (Siamese) twins.
and akko. Some say it is an ibex.
and dishon. One of the types of re'em (oryx).
and te'o. Some say it is one of the extinct cattle species, and some hold that it is the bison.
and zamer. Some wrote that it is the giraffe.
wild ox. Some estimate that it is the water buffalo.
and the meri. Some estimate that it is the zebu or African cattle.
and its blood requires covering. The laws of covering the blood are detailed in Hilchot Shechitah chapter 14.
its fat is punishable by karet. The laws of fat are detailed below, chapter 7.
they are by oral tradition. They were received by tradition and are not explicit in the Torah.
branching. Additional branches, as it were, split off from the horn.
curved. Bent.
and notched. They have a groove.
the notch is hidden in them. So that it looks as if a bone were wrapped around the horn.
and spiraled. Coiled (according to the Commentary on the Mishnah, Chullin 3:6), and there are other explanations.
until they are on the horns. Only if it has all three signs is it certainly a wild animal, even if its horns are not branching.
and the keresh, even though it has only one horn. Some identified the keresh with the giraffe, which has a bony protuberance like a horn on its forehead, and has all the signs of purity.
rather he listed only impure species etc. The Torah specified the forbidden species only, from which it follows that other species of birds are permitted.
and the forbidden species are twenty-four. And they are listed in the list of impure birds in the book of Leviticus (11:13-19) and Deuteronomy (14:12-18).
and it is the ra'ah mentioned in Deuteronomy. It is the same species, but called by another name in the parallel list.
expert in these species and their names. Identifies the birds and knows the names of their species.
and a pure bird is eaten by tradition, and it must be a well-known matter etc. That everyone in that place accepts that this bird is pure.
my master the hunter. The teacher who taught me to hunt.
and the crop, which is the mur'ah. A kind of pouch at the bottom of the bird's esophagus in which food stays and softens.
its gizzard can be peeled by hand. Its inner layer can be separated from it, and is not firmly attached to it.
it was hard and stuck. The layers of the gizzard were pressed tightly to one another.
one that has one sign. That has only one of the signs mentioned above in halacha 16.
that spreads its feet when a thread is stretched for it. That when it stands on the thread it places two toes on each side.
and any that dwells with the impure ones and resembles them. A bird that nests together with the impure ones and resembles them somewhat.
the kinds of locusts that the Torah permitted. The list of pure locusts appears in Leviticus 11:22.
and the hunter is trusted regarding them like a bird. To say that they are pure and that this is how his teacher taught him, as above halacha 15.
that cover. Cover.
legs. Hind legs.
and fish have two signs. The signs of fish are mentioned in the Torah in Leviticus 11:9-12 and Deuteronomy 14:9-10.
that glides. Swims.
attached to its whole body. On its skin.
that cover. Cover.

and a negative derived from a positive is a positive. A prohibition not stated in the Torah in negative language but learned from the implication of a positive formulation is not considered a negative commandment but a positive commandment.
for they are under a negative commandment. These animals are forbidden by a negative prohibition.

that have one sign. The camel, hare and hyrax bring up the cud but do not split the hoof, and the pig splits the hoof but does not bring up the cud, as stated in the verse there (and see further above 1:2-3).
in addition to the positive commandment derived from 'these you may eat'. Besides the positive prohibition mentioned in the previous paragraph.
and the verse did not distinguish between the flesh and fat of the impure animals. There is no separate negative prohibition for the fat, as there is for pure animals (see below 7:1).
a swarming flying creature. Flying swarming creatures, which the Torah forbade for eating.
from the swarming creatures of the earth. Swarmers that crawl on the ground.
such as the weasel, the tortoise, snakes etc. Among both the large species and the small ones.
and the eight swarming creatures mentioned in the Torah. Which the Torah specified as defiling (see Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot chapter 4).
one who eats the size of a lentil of their flesh. The size of a lentil.
according to the measure of their impurity. The eating measure was equated to the measure of their impurity, which is a lentil's size (ibid. 4:1-2).
and all of them combine with one another to a lentil's size. Pieces of swarming creatures smaller than a lentil combine, and if they total a lentil's size, the one who eats them is flogged.
when does this apply? When he ate of them after their death. Just as they defile at the size of a lentil only after death, so too they are forbidden for eating at this measure only after death.
he ate a whole limb etc. Although for impurity the measure of a limb from a defiling swarming creature is any amount (see Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 4:3).
it combines to a lentil's size. Also regarding impurity (Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 4:7).
the blood is attached to the flesh. That it did not come out of the flesh.

for its flesh is not distinct from its blood. There is no difference between them in law, since the blood too is forbidden as a swarming creature and has no separate prohibition, so they combine together.
and even though it does not defile. And therefore blood and flesh do not combine for impurity; nonetheless, for the prohibition of eating they combine.
from other swarming creatures that do not defile. For only the eight swarming creatures defile (ibid. halacha 14).
that separated and he gathered it. It came out of the flesh, and they collected it.
that they warned him for eating a swarming creature. They would warn the eater that the transgression is eating a swarming creature.
but only for the blood of an animal, wild animal and bird. Explained below 6:1.
and their disputes. The differences between the measures for the various matters.
and the dalfon. Dolphin.
that are not created from male and female but from dung that rotted and the like. Worms and the like, which they thought are formed from rot and mold and not from the union of male and female.
even though they do not procreate. That this distinction is not significant for the prohibition of eating (and compare Hilchot Shabbat 11:2).
separated and went out to the ground. Emerged from the fruit or food to the earth.
but if they did not separate, it is permitted to eat the fruit and the worm inside it. For it never swarmed on the ground.
for a worm in it does not survive twelve months. Therefore if he found a worm, it is certain that the food became wormy after it was detached from the ground.
separated into the air. That emerged from the fruit into the air.
part of them to the ground. That only part of the worm's body touched the ground.
on the pit from inside. That separated from the flesh of the fruit.

a worm found in the innards of fish or in the brain in the head... is forbidden. We must assume that those worms came from outside into the fish and animals (Maggid Mishneh). Some wrote that it refers to worms formed inside the fish or animal, which in life are considered like fruits attached to the ground (Rada'a).
for they are like fruit that became wormy after being detached. That it surely got there after the fish died.
the water in vessels. Stored in containers, and considered detached from the ground.
that it has. Signs.
in pools. Bodies of water.
collected. Gathered.
and stoops. Bends down.
to the walls of. Walls.
permitted. Because that is its way, so the walls too are considered its place of growth, and it is as though it did not separate.
as we explained. Above halacha 17.
that which we said in this chapter, one who eats an olive's bulk. Everywhere in the chapter where the eating measure of an olive's bulk is discussed.
an olive's bulk from a large creature. Such a measure from an animal whose flesh is more than an olive's bulk.
an impure creature in itself, entirely. In its entirety.
than a mustard seed. A mustard seed, a tiny measure.
while alive. While it is alive.
that even one of its legs is missing. So that it is no longer a whole creature.
one who eats a whole fly... is flogged for a flying swarming creature. As above halacha 5.
that it had wings. And it is therefore considered a flying swarming creature.
and it walks on the ground like other swarming creatures. And it is considered a swarming creature of the earth (above halacha 6).
and it was mostly in the water. It lives in water or swims in it, and is therefore also judged as a water swarming creature (above halacha 12).
of the species that were created in fruit. That separated from the fruit, and are also forbidden under 'the swarming creature that swarms on the earth' (above halacha 14).
and if it was of the species that procreate. That it is also forbidden because of 'and every creature that swarms upon the earth is an abomination' (above halacha 13).
and if it was among the impure birds. That it is a large, developed swarming creature like a bird, and forbidden also as an impure bird (above halacha 4).

and one for eating a k'zayit of the carcass of impure animals. Of the flesh of creeping creatures, because of the general prohibition that applies to all creeping things, “Do not make yourselves abominable through any swarming thing that swarms” (above, halacha 12); the multiple lashes for eating creeping things apply only to a whole creature that has not been crushed (Orah veSimchah).
as it is said, and the daughter of the ostrich. In the prohibition of impure birds.
and the same applies to anything forbidden like the ostrich. That is, any impure animal.
and to all things similar to an egg. Any food that comes out of their bodies.
we already explained. Above 2:3.
for it is a positive commandment. Only, with no negative commandment and lashes as with the ostrich; therefore what comes from it is permitted (Orah veSimchah).
that is not the essence of their bodies. It was not formed from substances digested in them.
they gather. They collect.
like one who nurses from a creeping thing. Which is an abominable thing.
and stopped. Stopped nursing.
because of his health and not because of illness. That he stopped nursing while healthy and not because of sickness.
who was weaned after twenty-four months. That is the proper duration of nursing (and see Hilchot Ishut 21:16, Hilchot Gerushin 11:26).
as one who eats half a measure. For it is forbidden by Torah law to eat less than the minimum amount for liability, even though there are no lashes for it (below 4:16).
in a cluster. The ovaries of a bird, which look like a cluster and from which eggs hang at various stages of development.
to develop. To form.
he is flogged for eating a creeping thing of the fowl. And not for eating an impure bird, since its formation was not yet complete.
the egg of a pure bird in which the chick began to develop etc.. The Sages forbade it because it resembles a creeping thing that crawls on the ground.
a bit. A little.
spoiled. Rotten.
the generous spirit. One who is not fastidious.
a chick that was born... it is permitted to eat it. After slaughter, since it is considered a full bird.
that became a treifah. That became a treifah (for the definition of this term see below 4:6-9).
the bird died as a carcass. It died other than by valid slaughter.
if a complete egg is found in it... it is permitted. Since the egg was fully formed before the bird became a carcass, it is not considered part of the bird but a separate thing.
a chick from the egg of a treifah. That hatched from an egg laid by a bird that is a treifah.
for its kind is not impure. Since it came out of the egg, it is no longer considered part of the body of the treifah.
in the first batch. The first laying after it became a treifah.
the first ones are permitted. Since it conceived and laid again, it is proven that it is not a treifah, for a treifah cannot do so (Hilchot Shechitah 11:1).
the milk of an impure animal does not curdle. It lacks the properties that allow it to coagulate and solidify into cheese.
the whey. The liquid remaining from milk after it is made into cheese.
with the skin of the stomach. A piece from the wall of the stomach, which contains a substance that makes milk curdle.
and why does it not become nullified in a minority. As in the law of an ordinary mixture of a forbidden substance in a permitted one (as detailed below 15:1-6).
as will be explained. Below 9:16, 16:26.
in fruit juices such as fig sap, and they are recognizable in the cheese. It can be identified in the cheese itself that these substances, which are permitted, were used.
the dregs of milk that remain in it. Remnants of gentile milk mixed in the butter.
it is not mixed with the butter. For it is solid and the milk is liquid.
and cooked it until the dregs of milk were gone. Heated it until the liquids evaporated.
gentiles' scalded vessels. What was cooked in gentiles' vessels, in which the taste of forbidden food has been absorbed.
as will be explained. Below 17:18.
whose two ends are like a jar's. Both of its ends are rounded like the wide base of a jar.
whose two ends are sharp. Having a pointed end.
relies on it. See this law also above 1:15.
and we do not worry that perhaps they are eggs of a treifah. Eggs that were laid by a bird that is a treifah, for this is not common.
scrambled eggs. Mixed together, not whole in their shells.
I salt them and take them out of a pure fish. For with salted fish eggs it is not apparent which fish they came from.
that have no sign. Signs of kashrut (and this refers only to the fish; see below 11:25 and the text there).
but in the Land of Israel. See also below 8:8 (regarding the sciatic nerve) and 11:25 (regarding wine).

and milk may be bought from any Israelite anywhere. Since one can easily stand over the gentile while he milks and see that he is milking a pure animal, they were not suspected of selling forbidden milk (Maggid Mishneh).
their brine. The liquid in which the fish were pickled.
a pure fish swims in it. Is found in it; in this case we assume that all the brine is brine of pure fish.
a trough. A small boat.
all are permitted. Since they are open they are considered one barrel.
crushed. Pulverized.
a large jar. A large jug.
and anything not properly slaughtered is a carcass. Even if it was slaughtered, it is considered as if it died on its own.
and it will be explained in the laws of slaughter. Chapters 1-4.
pure species only. Pure domestic animals, wild animals and birds.
any amount. Even if it is very small, since he ate all of it.
he is flogged for eating a carcass. For the bird died immediately when it swallowed it.
and if he ate it after it died, until there is a k'zayit in it. In which case it is judged as ordinary carcass meat, and not as a creature.
since there is a k'zayit in all of it. Together with the skin and bones.
a miscarried animal. A dead fetus.
until the night of the eighth. The beginning of the eighth day from its birth.
it is permitted on the day it was born. For it is known that it is not a nefel.
and you cannot say that it was mauled and killed it. One should not interpret treifah as one that died because it was mauled, for one that died is forbidden as a carcass.
and the kid dragged with its leg, tail or ear. These are not fatal injuries.
and flesh in the field that is torn. The verse continues: “you shall not eat it; you shall throw it to the dogs.”
the verse speaks of the usual case. It speaks of an example from common cases.
it was mauled in the courtyard. And not in the field.
and the meaning of the verse. The intent of the verse.
anything like which cannot live. Nothing like it is capable of living.
and it will be explained in the laws of slaughter. Chapters 5-11.
and likewise one who cuts flesh from a living animal. A piece of flesh; but if he cut off a whole limb, he is liable for a limb from a living animal (below 5:1-2).
since the animal became like flesh in the field. Not through slaughter and not through death.
because its strength weakened and it is about to die etc.. Because of bodily weakness, and not because of injury to one of its limbs.
that convulsed at the end of slaughter. This is a sign that it was alive, as explained in the following halachot.
and this matter is not a prohibition etc.. It does not count as treifah or carcass, but is only a custom of stringency and beautifying the commandment.
the dangerously ill one. Very sick.
any that is stood up and does not stand. That one lifts up and it falls because of its illness.
even though it eats the food of a healthy animal. Even if it eats the food of healthy animals, this is no sign that it is healthy.
that stretched out its foreleg and returned it. Straightened the foreleg and bent it again.
that stretched out its leg. Straightened its hind leg.
for this is not a convulsion but the departure of the soul. This movement is not a sign of life.
twitched. Made a slight movement.
do not combine with one another. To complete the minimum amount for liability (see also below 14:5).
as will be explained there. Hilchot Nezirut 5:3.
one who eats half a measure. For it is forbidden by Torah law to eat less than the minimum amount for liability, and one is not flogged for this eating, but receives disciplinary lashes (below 14:2).
and a carcass combines with a treifah. As will be explained at the end of the halacha.
carcass flesh with the flesh of an impure animal do not combine. Because these are two different prohibitions.
and half a k'zayit of flesh from a living pure animal. Which is forbidden as a carcass (above, halacha 10).
two names. Two prohibitions.
as we explained. Above 2:1-4.
and a treifah is the beginning of a carcass. For a treifah leads to death.

from places from which blood spurts when they are cut from their hide. He ate from the horns, hooves or nails in the part close to the flesh, from which blood comes out when they are separated from the skin.
the stomach contents of a carcass and of an impure animal. The food remains found inside the animal's stomach (see also below 9:15).
the skin of the stomach. A piece from the wall of the stomach.
the skin that comes opposite the face of a donkey. A kind of membrane that wraps it at birth.
excrement. Waste, feces.
a settled-area pig. A domesticated pig.
the hump of a camel. The hump.
and had not yet reached carrying age. That is not yet at the age at which burdens are loaded on it.
the pudendum. The female genital organ.
the fetus. The embryo.
the anakah, the koach, the leta'ah and the chomet. Which are among the eight creeping creatures that cause impurity (above 2:7).
with a stoned ox. An ox that killed a person and is sentenced to stoning (Hilchot Nizkei Mamon 10:1).
and it is a carcass. And it is forbidden to eat even without this.
and if he preceded and slaughtered it properly, it is forbidden to benefit from. And from eating, in general.
it may not be sold, nor given to dogs or to gentiles. Unlike carcass meat, which may be fed to dogs or sold to a gentile (see below 8:15-17).
and the excrement of a stoned ox is permitted for benefit. The feces, which are not part of its body (as above, halachot 19-20).
for example, if its witnesses were proven false. It became clear that they testified falsely, and it is not to be stoned.
goes out and grazes with the herd. It is like an ordinary ox, and is permitted for eating and benefit.
and if it became known after it was stoned, it is permitted for benefit. Like any carcass.
they learned from tradition. From the tradition of the Sages.
to forbid a limb cut from a living animal. From a living creature.
and regarding a limb from a living animal, it was said to Noah etc.. That is, this is one of the prohibitions that apply to all human beings, gentiles included (see Hilchot Melachim chapter 9).
both a limb that has flesh... and a limb that has no bone. In all of them the prohibition of a limb from a living animal applies.
that it extends as in its creation. As it is when attached to the animal.
as we explained. Above 4:10.
and even if he ate a whole limb etc.. Although the limb is whole, it does not have the law of a creature, for which one is liable even for less than a k'zayit (compare above 2:21).
and separated. Divided and detached.
and if not, he is exempt. Since the limb is not as in its creation, the sinews and bones do not combine with the flesh.
and it became a treifah by its removal. The absence of that limb defines it as a treifah.

he is liable for two... for the two prohibitions come at once. Although ordinarily one prohibition does not take effect on another, when both prohibitions come at once, both take effect (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8).

one who tears fat from a living animal and eats it is flogged twice. For the prohibition of a limb from a living animal applies also to the descendants of Noah (above 5:1) and takes effect on the prohibition of fat because it is an “added prohibition” (for its definition see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8).
the dangling one. One cut off for the most part but still slightly attached.
if it cannot return and live. That it cannot be that it will mend and heal.
that did not separate until after it was slaughtered, it is forbidden. That it was completely detached from the body only after the slaughter; it was not permitted by the slaughter.
as if it fell while alive. As if it was severed from the animal during its life.
pulled loose. Pulled it to detach it from the body.
the testicles. The testes.
that he crushed or detached. Without separating them from the body.
therefore it does not rot. The limb did not decay, which proves that it still has life.
that all Israel practiced from before. Since ancient times.
covers. Covers.
the bone protrudes outside. That the flesh and skin do not cover it.
shattered. Smashed to fragments.
or was eaten away like flesh that the doctor scrapes. Rotten flesh, which is removed so that the place can heal.
the majority is gathered from many places. It is composed of small parts that together complete most of its thickness and circumference.
that was cut around. Cut around.
that the flesh was scraped from above etc.. The top layer was removed from it.
pieces of the fetus or its limb are permitted. For as long as it has not come out, it is permitted by the slaughter of the mother (below, halachot 13-14).
a fetus that put out its hand or leg. Outside the womb, and afterward its mother was slaughtered.
for any flesh that came outside its boundary. Came outside its permitted area, which is the animal's body.
becomes forbidden like flesh that separated from a living animal. That was cut from its body, which is not permitted by its slaughter.
as we explained. Above 4:10.

even if only the minority of it remained, the part that came out is forbidden and the part inside is permitted. Only the part that came out is forbidden as a treifah, and the minority of the limb is not drawn after the majority.
cut off what came out of the limb. Cut off the part that protruded.
and cut it while it is outside... the place of the cut is forbidden etc.. The part of the stump facing outward.
cuts again. Another piece of the same limb.
a limb from a living animal. And not the prohibition of treifah.
and if it was cut after slaughter, one who eats it is not flogged. For a limb from a living animal. Although it is forbidden as a treifah (above, halacha 9), one is not flogged for that.
and even if the fetus died. For as long as it has not come out, it is considered alive along with its mother.
since it comes from the general category of limbs. The fat is formed from the body of the animal as a whole unit, and the forbidden limb is included in this as well.
like the fat of a treifah. Which is forbidden as something that comes from an impure animal (above 3:10).
fetus. Embryo.
and even the placenta is permitted to eat. For when the fetus was permitted by the slaughter of the mother, the placenta was permitted with it.

a fetus that was in it went away. That it had another fetus in it that dissolved; and if part of it came out, it is possible that the fetus was in that part, and it is considered to have given birth to it before the slaughter, and the placenta is not permitted for eating.
the slaughter of its mother purifies it. Makes its flesh fit.
and if it set its hooves on the ground. It stood on its hooves and walked (see also Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 2:7).
tore the animal. Not by valid slaughter.
and the slaughter of its mother does not help it. Since its mother's slaughter is not valid slaughter.
and if its months were not completed, it is forbidden. If the months of gestation were not completed, it is forbidden even if the fetus itself is slaughtered.
any fetus that put out its head and returned it etc.. For putting out the head is considered a complete birth (see also Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 10:6, Hilchot Bikkurim 11:15).
a fixed sin offering. One that always comes from an animal, unlike the “rising and falling” offering, which varies according to a person's financial state (see Hilchot Shegagot 1:4).
and you shall not eat any blood. Including impure animals.
deer, gazelle and yachmur. Which are of the category of wild animals.
collected it in a vessel and drank it. Collected it in a vessel; it is permitted even though it looks like eating forbidden blood.
the essence of their bodies. Extracted from their bodies.
like the milk of an impure animal. Which is forbidden to eat (above 3:1).
as we explained. Above 2:9-10.
if it separated. If it came out of the body.
blood of the teeth. That is found between the teeth.

karet applies only to blood that comes out at the time of slaughter etc.. For all of these are defined as “blood in which the soul departs,” for the eating of which one is liable to karet (below, halacha 4).
and neck-stabbing. Killing not by slaughter but by stabbing with a knife.
blood of bloodletting. That was taken from the animal in a medical procedure.
as long as it spurts. As long as it flows strongly.
blood of drainage. The blood that flows after the soul has departed.
and blood that gathers in the heart at the time of slaughter. For at the time of slaughter, blood is drawn from the limbs into the heart.
the fetus. Embryo.
whether for roasting or for a pot. There is no difference in this law whether he intends to roast it over fire or cook it in a pot.
cuts it open and removes its blood. He must cut the heart and remove the blood gathered in it.
salts it. The act of salting causes the meat to release the blood within it. For the manner of salting see below, halacha 10.
cuts it open after cooking it and it is permitted. For the heart's flesh is smooth and does not absorb blood.
and if he did not cut it open, one is not liable to karet for it. For the blood inside the heart does not have the amount of a k'zayit.
cut it and threw it into vinegar or into boiling water. This action (called below “scalding”) seals the meat and prevents it from releasing the blood in it.
until it whitens. Becomes white.
it is permitted to cook it. For the vinegar or boiling water caused the liver's blood not to come out in cooking.
to singe it over the fire. To roast it slightly over the flame.
a widespread custom. That spread among the public.
the whole pot is forbidden. Everything in the pot is forbidden, since the liver releases blood into the dish.
and it is permitted to roast liver with meat on one spit. And they are placed vertically.
so that the liver is below. So that the blood coming out of the liver does not flow onto the meat.
the spleen... for it is not blood but flesh that resembles blood. And its law is like any flesh.

one who breaks the neck of an animal before its soul departs etc.. He slaughtered an animal, and before it died he broke its neck, causing the life-blood not to come out in a spurt but to remain inside and be absorbed in the limbs.
and it is forbidden to eat raw meat from it, even if he scalded it etc.. Although raw meat is permitted by scalding or salting (below, halacha 12), here cutting and salting specifically are required.
we already explained. Above 4:13.
the meat does not come out of its blood etc.. It is not fully cleansed of blood.
and rinses it. Washes it in water.
the time it takes to walk a mil. The time it takes an average person to walk two thousand cubits, about a kilometer.
so that it whitens immediately and no blood comes out. Scalding is necessary so that blood will not be released from it afterward.
to shake off. To shake out.
in a perforated vessel. So that the blood drains down and the meat does not soak in it.
for roasting he salts and roasts immediately. Without waiting for the meat to sit in its salt.
and if he scalded it in vinegar. He put it in vinegar to block the blood from coming out.
he may not scald in it a second time. For its strength has weakened.
it and the vinegar are forbidden until he salts. Since the piece turned red, we assume that the blood was not sealed inside the meat but was released into the vinegar.
in the kelaf. The membrane, which can also be peeled off (see below 7:14).
the large veins. Large blood vessels.
and its place of slaughter. The place of slaughter.
for the blood gathers into it. The blood collects in the cavity of the skull and is absorbed in the brain.
to receive its juices. That drip from it during roasting, in order to use them.
throws a little salt into the vessel. Which helps the blood collect at the bottom of the vessel.
until it is roasted. Until the fat is clear and the blood settles at the bottom.
it is permitted to eat it. For the liquid that dripped from the roasted meat onto the bread is not blood.
fish... that he salted. In order to prepare them for eating, not that fish must be salted by law.
because the fish is soft. Tender.

and even though he salted them very well. For the meat releases blood even if salted, as long as it was not scalded in boiling water on all sides (see above, halacha 10), and the stuffing does not allow the boiling water to seal the blood inside the meat properly.
and if he roasted them, they are permitted. For the fire draws out the blood, and scalding is not needed (see above, halacha 12).
for we do not assume that there is blood in the intestines. We do not assume there is blood there, and they do not require salting (see also below 7:15).
that he coated them. Covered them.
and roasted them. Without salting and scalding.
even if the coating reddened etc.. Even if the coating turned red, it is permitted to eat it.
because it is coarse flour that crumbles and the blood comes out. Because the grains of the semolina are large, all the blood comes out through the gaps in the dough.
with wheat flour that he soaked. That he washed the wheat before grinding, and the dough is solid and the blood does not come out of it at all.
white as silver, one may eat from it. Completely white, which proves that no blood came out.
with other flours. That are neither hard nor very crumbly.
it is forbidden to eat with it hot. Ideally, because of the blood that comes out at the time of slaughter.
until he whitens it etc.. These are the usual ways of making a knife fit for use (see below 17:7).
a radish or the like, of sharp things. Which because of their sharpness absorb from the blood on the knife (for a similar law see below 9:24).
coated with lead. Smoothed with a lead coating.
in its shards. In the body of the bowl, which is made of clay.
fat. A part of the animal's fat that is defined as “chelev” for the purpose of the prohibition; below, halacha 5, the forbidden fats are detailed.
a fixed sin offering. One that always comes from an animal, unlike the “rising and falling” offering, which varies according to a person's financial state (see Hilchot Shegagot 1:4).
other domestic and wild animals... their fat is like their flesh. For fat has no distinct definition, and its law is like flesh, both for prohibition and permission.

since it is added. Since the prohibition of a carcass or treifah includes more than the prohibition of fat (for it applies to all the flesh), the fat is included with it and becomes forbidden through the additional prohibition (an “inclusive prohibition”; for its definition see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8; and see another example below 8:6).
one who slaughters an animal and finds a fetus in it. An embryo, which is permitted by the slaughter of its mother (see above 5:14).
all its fat is permitted... because it is like a limb of her. The whole fetus is like a limb of the animal, including its fat, and therefore it is not forbidden as fat.
its months were completed. That it completed in its mother's womb all the months of gestation.
that did not set its hooves on the ground and does not need slaughter etc.. See above 5:14.
and if its months were completed... its fat is forbidden. For once the months of pregnancy are completed, it is no longer considered a limb of the mother.
all the threads and membranes. See below, halacha 10.
he is liable for it as if he had cut it from the mother's own fat. And he is not considered as one who eats flesh from a living animal, but as one who eats fat.
for the months are what cause the prohibition of fat. As explained in the previous halacha.
the fat on the innards. Fats found on the entrails.
and that on the two kidneys. The layer of fat that wraps the kidneys.
and that on the loins. The walls of the animal's abdomen (the flanks), on which there are various fats. See the illustration on the next page.
but the fat tail. The tail of sheep, which is rich in fat.

the fat tail is called chelev only with regard to offerings. For in the matter of the portions of the offering offered on the altar, the fat tail is called chelev (see Leviticus 3:9), but it is not called chelev for the purpose of the prohibition. Just as the kidneys and the lobe of the liver are also called “fats” in the context of offering them on the altar (see Leviticus 3:16 and elsewhere), though they are certainly not included in the prohibition of eating fat.
for it is their best part. The choicest part.
the masos and the fat on the beit hakosot. Two of the stomach compartments of ruminants.
is the fat on the innards. In addition to the fat on the rumen itself, which is the main fat on the innards (see Hilchot Shechitah 6:11).
that is at the roots of the thighs on the inside. The place where the thighbones connect to the pelvic bones, on the side of the body cavity.
curved like a bow. The stomach is shaped like a bow, its outer side rounded and its inner side relatively straight.
and the threads in the fat. The threads of the loins and the thin threads on the innards; see below, halachot 10-11.
covers. Covers.
and likewise the fat on the kidneys is forbidden, but not what is inside the kidneys. For the fat wrapping the kidneys also enters into them.
a person removes the white inside the kidney... and need not dig after it. He removes most of the fat inside it and may eat the kidney, even though a little of the white remains in it.
two wicks of fat. Two long strips of fat.
it is forbidden. And it is part of the fat on the loins (above, halacha 6).
the thin, coiled ones. The digestive tubes from the stomach to the rectum.
the fat on the thin intestines is forbidden. It was included by the verse: “and all the fat that is on the innards” (Leviticus 3:3).
some of them because of fat. Threads that pass through forbidden fats, or membranes that are in contact with them.
and some of them because of blood. Threads that are blood vessels, or membranes within which blood vessels pass.
as we said. Above 6:10 (the manner of salting).
cut it. The thread (the vein) so that the blood gathered in it comes out.
for roasting he need not remove it. For the fire draws out the blood.
there are five threads in the loins. Threads passing through the flesh of the walls of the animal's abdomen.
the foreleg. The front leg.
like a spider's web, entangled with one another. A dense system of blood vessels, like spider webs.
and the membrane on the brain... and the membrane on the testicles. For within these membranes there are many blood threads.
that has not completed thirty days. Since its birth.
until he peels. The membrane, within which the blood threads pass.
as we explained. Above 5:10.
we do not assume that they contain blood. We do not assume there is blood there, and they need neither cutting nor salting (see above 6:18).
and they are like half a measure. Their law is similar to half a measure, for which, though it is forbidden by Torah law, there are no lashes (below 14:2).
fats are not salted etc.. So that the fat is not absorbed into the meat.
one in which he slaughters. See above 6:20.
the sciatic nerve. See below chapter 8.
remove it. From its function.
even in many places. That the k'zayit of fat is not concentrated in one place.
because the butcher is trusted regarding fat. Every such case is treated stringently, because people rely on the butchers' trustworthiness regarding removal of the fat from the meat.
sacred animals that are not eaten. Whose meat is offered on the altar, or burned outside the Temple, and is not eaten.

the hip socket... but the rest of the nerve etc.. The sciatic nerve emerges from the spinal cord and descends along the hind legs to their end. Only the section of the nerve on the “hip socket” (for its definition see Hilchot Shechitah 10:3, in the explanation) is forbidden by Torah law, and all the rest is rabbinic.
the fat on the nerve. The fat covering the nerve along its whole length.
and the upper one. The one that is not adjacent to the bone.
and if he ate the whole nerve on the socket. In its entirety.
as a creature in its own right. For which one is flogged even if it does not have the amount of a k'zayit (above 2:21).
is flogged eighty. For each k'zayit measure, or a nerve in its creation, he is flogged forty.

that has no hip socket, but its thigh is round. So it is in many manuscripts, and the text is difficult, for the thigh of a bird is not round but long, as explained later in the halacha (and so he also wrote in the Commentary on the Mishnah, Chullin 7:1). Some versions read “but its thigh is long,” meaning that the thigh of a bird is not like the hip socket of a person or domestic animal, which are round.
exempt. He is not flogged either for eating impure meat or for the sciatic nerve.
for nerves are not part of the flesh. For they are not fit for food.
as we explained. Above 4:18.
liable for two. For the nerve, and for a carcass, treifah or burnt offering (for the prohibition of eating a burnt offering see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 11:1).

in the prohibition of the rest of its body that was permitted. For the added prohibition of a carcass, treifah or burnt offering includes the rest of the body, and therefore the nerve too is included in this prohibition, and an additional prohibition applies to it (an “inclusive prohibition”; for its definition see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8; for another example see above 7:2).
just as he is trusted regarding fat. Above 7:21.
but in the Land of Israel. See above 3:21 for this law regarding dairy products.
and they excommunicate. Place under a ban (for the details of the ban see Hilchot Talmud Torah 7:2-4, and there 6:14 for the list of all those who are banned).
to buy. To purchase.

and returns a lost item of significant value etc.. That he found a valuable item and returned it and did not take it for himself, which proves that he has repented and is no longer eager for money (see also Hilchot Shechitah 10:14).
and their maidservants. Their female slaves.
it is forbidden. Perhaps he bought it from the gentiles' store.
meat found thrown in the market, follow the majority. Since it was thrown among them, its nature is decided by the majority.
and disappeared from sight. That it was not seen for some time.
tied. Bound.
permitted for benefit. For use other than eating.
its place is recognizable. And one sees that the nerve was not removed.
in the way that it specified regarding a carcass... and fat. In which the verse specified that though they are forbidden to eat, other uses are permitted.
from tradition. The tradition of the Sages.
and the proceeds are permitted. It is permitted to use the money given in exchange for the forbidden item.
and to direct his work toward forbidden things. That this should not be his profession, but only occasional, as below, halacha 17.
with milk that a gentile milked... and gentiles' cheese. See above 3:13-14 for the detailed laws.
and they bury it. So that no one will ever benefit from it.
and its ashes are forbidden. If the food was burned, even the ashes are forbidden to benefit from (see also Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 19:13).
like the ashes of all those that are buried. For the list of those buried see there 19:11.

the verse did not remain silent about forbidding eating etc.. The prohibition of eating meat and milk cooked together is not mentioned explicitly in the Torah, since it is self-evident from the fact that even cooking them together is forbidden.

just as it was silent about forbidding the daughter etc.. The prohibition of relations with one's daughter is not mentioned explicitly in the Torah, only the prohibition of relations with a daughter's daughter or a son's daughter, and it is self-evident that relations with one's daughter are forbidden (see also Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:6).
and “kid” includes the offspring of the ox etc.. “Kid” is a general term for all the young of domestic animals.
until it specifies and says “a kid of the goats”. Only if it is written explicitly “a kid of the goats” does it not mean other kinds.

and “a kid in its mother's milk” is said only because the verse speaks of the usual case. The reason it says “in its mother's milk,” even though the prohibition applies to the milk of any pure animal, is that the verse gives an example from common cases.
it is permitted to cook and permitted for benefit. For they were not included in the prohibition. Of course, eating them is forbidden because of the meat or milk that comes from an impure animal.
so that the people will not extend. So that they will not expand beyond what is permitted.

for the verse implies only a kid in its mother's milk literally etc.. Since from the plain meaning of the verse one could understand that the prohibition applies only to a kid in its mother's milk. So that it be clear that the verse does not mean this, the Sages forbade any mixture of pure meat and milk.
fish and locusts may be eaten with milk. The Sages did not decree on these, which are not considered meat at all.
complete eggs. That were completed with white and yolk.
one is not flogged for it. If he cooked it thus in milk, for this is not considered cooking.
in whey. The liquids remaining after milk becomes cheese (Commentary on the Mishnah, Machshirin 6:5).
in the milk of a dead animal. That came out of the animal after it died.

for there is neither an inclusive prohibition etc. here. For if there were one of these, a prohibition would take effect on a prohibition (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8). And although meat and milk are also forbidden to benefit from, so that there would seem to be an added prohibition, since the prohibition of benefit is learned from the prohibition of eating, it is included in it, and since the prohibition of eating does not take effect (for it is neither inclusive nor added), the prohibition of benefit also does not take effect (Commentary on the Mishnah, Keritot 3:4).
inclusive prohibition. That the prohibition applies to additional things, which include the forbidden item (for examples see above 7:2; there 8:6).
added prohibition. That the additional prohibition adds a stringency beyond the first prohibition (for examples see below 14:18-19; Hilchot Terumot 10:25).
a one-time prohibition. That the two prohibitions took effect simultaneously (for examples see above 2:1, 5:5, Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 11:9).
one who cooks a fetus etc.. A fetus found alive in the innards of a slaughtered animal, which has the law of its mother's meat (above 5:13).
one who cooks a placenta or skin... is exempt. Because they are not fit for eating (above 4:18).

but if he did not remove it, it is estimated by sixty. For if the piece stayed in the pot and released the forbidden milk it had absorbed, the pot cannot be judged by imparting taste, since the forbidden milk has no taste distinguishable from the rest of the milk in the pot, and it has the law of a kind in its own kind, whose measure is sixty (see below 15:1-6).
into a pot of meat. On one of the pieces of meat.

even though if the piece were squeezed no taste would remain in it. Although if the milk came out of the piece and was released into the whole dish and nullified in it, no taste of milk would remain in the piece.
and it is estimated by all of it. The whole piece is considered forbidden, and sixty times its size is needed.
in what case is this said. That it is estimated by sixty against the piece.

when he did not stir the pot at first when the milk fell, but only at the end, and did not cover it. That he did not mix the dish or close the pot with a lid, and in that time the taste of milk was absorbed in the piece and did not immediately mix into the whole pot.
if he stirred from the beginning to the end etc.. So that the milk was immediately mixed into the whole pot.
it is judged by imparting taste. We check whether the whole pot has the taste of milk.
milk fell into the gravy. Into the sauce between the pieces.
he stirs the whole pot until everything is mixed etc.. He mixes it well, and it is estimated against the whole pot.
estimated by sixty. For it is treated as a kind in its own kind (see also below 15:30).
and if he cooked, by imparting taste. If the meat vessel imparted taste to the milk, it is forbidden.
the udder. The animal's udder.
in the milk of a slaughtered animal. The milk that was in the udder came out after the death of the animal, and is not the milk that prohibits by Torah law.
as we explained. Above 5:6.
that he cut open. Cut it.
and cleaned out. Removed completely.
warp and woof. Lengthwise and crosswise.
and smeared it against the wall. Pressed it against the wall to squeeze out the milk absorbed in it.
and the udder is counted in the number. The udder itself is included in the sixty as a piece of permitted meat.

and either way. Whether its prohibition was already nullified in sixty in a permitted pot, or its prohibition was not nullified in a permitted pot, it prohibits a pot that does not have sixty against its prohibition.
and it is estimated by sixty as with the first. For in this case too the udder itself is counted in the sixty.
as it is at the time it was cooked. Even though it shrank somewhat from cooking.
above the meat on a spit. Because milk drips from the udder onto the meat.
a stomach that he cooked with the milk in it. Milk that the animal nursed before it was slaughtered and that is still in its stomach.
it is like excrement, for it changes in the intestines. Its law is like other excrement (as above 4:20), because it is digested, and is not considered milk.
to curdle cheese with the skin of the stomach. To curdle with a piece from the wall of the stomach.
for the curdling agent. The stomach skin that curdles the cheese.
a permitted thing. That is not forbidden to eat in itself, for it is kosher meat, but is forbidden to mix with milk.

the cheese became forbidden because of carcass. Even if the taste of the stomach is not noticeable in the cheese, for a curdling agent that is a forbidden substance prohibits in any amount (see also below 16:26).
as we explained. Above 3:13.

or if hot fell into hot or cold into hot. If both are hot and cook together, or even if the hot is below and the cold falls into it, the heat of the lower one prevails and heats the cold upper one, and the entire food becomes forbidden.

but if one of them fell and it was hot etc.. If the cold is below and the hot falls into it, the coolness of the lower one prevails and cools the hot upper one, and therefore it is forbidden only to the extent of its outer layer (kelipah).
to bundle. To pack together.
salted food that cannot be eaten because of its salt. Food salted so much that it cannot be eaten because of its saltiness.
it is like hot. It is considered like a hot cooked dish and prohibits, even though it is cold.
kutach. A food made of whey, bread crumbs and salt.
in milk or in kutach. Cold.
rinses it and it is permitted. He washes off the milk that stuck to it (as above, halacha 17).
in slits. Cracks in the flesh of the bird, in which the taste of milk was absorbed.
that was seasoned with spices. Which also causes absorption of taste.
to bring the bird up with the cheese to the table. To place them together on the same table.
for fowl in milk is forbidden by rabbinic law. Above, halacha 4.
two guests at an inn. Guests in a lodging.
whose heart is not so familiar with the other as to eat with him. There is no close relationship between them, and they will not come to eat of each other's food.
one does not knead dough with milk etc.. To bake bread from it, lest the bread be eaten with meat.
and one does not coat the oven with fat tail. It is forbidden to smear it with animal fat.
until he heats the oven. And the fat burns off.
until it is recognizable. So that it will be clear that it is meat or dairy bread.
with the roast. Together in one oven.
a bowl in which they ate meat. And it absorbed the taste of the meat.
and cooked fish in it. And the fish received the taste of meat from the bowl, not directly from the meat.
in kutach. A dairy food; see above, halacha 18.
of sharp things. Which because of their sharpness absorb the taste of meat from the knife.
a cucumber or watermelon. Which are not sharp.
scrapes the place of the cut. Which has meat fat from the knife on it.
kamach. Kutach.
because it draws from it. The salt draws taste from the kutach and becomes dairy.
that he wash his hands and wipe his mouth. He must wash his hands and clean his mouth of the remains of the dairy foods.
fowl meat... he need not. For its prohibition is rabbinic (as explained above, halacha 4), and because its flesh is not so similar to the flesh of animals, they did not enact this precaution for it.
enough for the length of another meal. The time of waiting until the next meal.
about. Approximately.
the meat between the teeth that is not removed by wiping. Meat remains stuck between the teeth that do not come out by wiping (unlike a dairy food, for which wiping helps, as above, halacha 26).
all the prohibitions we mentioned. In the previous nine chapters.
of the seed of the earth. Things from the plant kingdom.
from the five species of grain. Wheat, barley, spelt, rye and oats.
from its new. From the new crop of that year.
until the omer is offered. For the laws of offering the omer see Hilchot Temidin uMusafin 7:3-13.
and parched grain. Roasted kernels.
and carmel. Fresh kernels.
whether in the time of the Temple. While the Temple stands.
noon. Midday.
they delay. They are late.
who keep two days. Who observe two days of Yom Tov because of doubt about the date (Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 5:4-5).
the seventeenth of Nisan. The next day, which is the first day of Chol HaMoed in the Land.
from each one. Of these kinds of food.
from tradition. The tradition of the Sages.
grain that took root. Grew roots in the ground.
that was not completed. Whose growth was not completed.
grain that took root after the omer and he harvested it. And the omer did not permit it.
while the wheat is still in the ground. And has not yet taken root.
because they became null in the ground. From the moment they were sown in the ground, they become permitted only after they take root and the next omer passes over them.
therefore if he gathered some of them. Took the seeds out of the soil.

an ear that brought a third. That grew a third of its full size, and is considered ripe grain for several purposes (see Hilchot Terumot 2:10; Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 2:7 and others); and there is doubt regarding the addition, whether to treat it as grain that was permitted and sown and forbidden until the next omer, or as continued growth of the ear that was already permitted.
and it added. It continued to grow.
that were sown with the vine. Together with the seed of the vine, a grape seed.
both are forbidden. The vine, and the other seed that was sown with it.
that is, lest you be distanced and forbid both. For the word “tikdash” in the verse has the meaning of distancing.
and the two combine with each other. The two forbidden species combine to complete the measure of a k'zayit.
and in the laws of kilayim. Chapters 5-8.
but the prohibition of orlah outside the Land. Which is not included in the verse forbidding orlah, which speaks only of the Land of Israel.
a halacha given to Moses at Sinai etc.. It was handed down by tradition that only definite orlah is forbidden, while doubtful orlah is permitted.
and it will be explained in the laws of Ma'aser Sheni. 9:13, and chapter 10.

lands that David conquered. Places north of the Land of Israel, in the area that is called Syria even today, which, since he conquered them before completing the conquest of the Land of Israel, are not considered entirely like it (Hilchot Terumot 1:3).
a vineyard that is doubtful orlah. That the vineyard itself is in doubt, and not only the fruit sold near it, as in the previous halacha.
hidden. Concealed.
permitted for benefit etc.. We do not worry that it is from this vineyard and forbidden as orlah.
the years of orlah. The three forbidden years.
it is permitted. Since according to the condition they were not partners in the fruit until now.
provided they do not come to an accounting. Even when they stipulated, they must take care that they not come to make a reckoning between them.
like one who exchanges orlah fruit. That he received something in exchange for it and benefited from orlah fruit.
neta revai. The fruit of the fourth year, whose law is to be eaten in Jerusalem, or to be redeemed and eaten with the redemption money in Jerusalem (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 9:1-2).
for they said only orlah. Applies outside the Land.
which will be explained in the laws of Ma'aser Sheni. 9:1.
that a vineyard of the fourth year alone. That only in a vineyard does the law of neta revai apply outside the Land.
and this matter has no basis. It has no foundation.
and it will be explained in the laws of Ma'aser Sheni. Chapter 9.
in the present time. Since when there is no Temple it is impossible to eat them in Jerusalem (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 2:1).
even for one perutah. For in the present time it is permitted to redeem them even not at their true value (see ibid. 2:2).
and throws that perutah into the Dead Sea. He throws it into the sea so that it is lost and others will not use it.
until the fifth year enters. Until the next year of the tree begins.
an error in ruling. A ruling of halacha that is incorrect.
and the verse misled them. The verse stated on the matter misled them, and they interpreted it incorrectly.

and the meaning of the verse is only that in the fifth year you shall eat its fruit. The meaning of the verse is that the fruit of the fifth year need not be redeemed at all, and is entirely ordinary, and not that one must wait until the fifth year to eat the fruit.
and one need not worry about this ruling. There is no need to be concerned and be stringent according to their opinion.
they shall not treat them as ordinary food. To eat them.
great terumah and terumat ma'aser. Separations from the crop that are given to the priests (for their definition see Hilchot Terumot 2:1, 3:12).
and caused them to bear the iniquity of guilt. One who treats tevel as ordinary food by eating it brings sin on himself.

tithes. The first tithe, given to the Levite (see Hilchot Ma'aser 1:1), the second tithe, eaten by the owners in Jerusalem, and sometimes the poor tithe is separated in place of the second tithe (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 1:1).
included in what was said, you may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain. And the prohibition regarding the tithes includes tevel, from which the tithes have not yet been separated.
and in the laws of terumot. Chapters 1-2.
and ma'asrot. Chapters 1-2.
except for wine and oil. Because the main way of using these fruits is to extract liquids from them (see for example Hilchot Terumot 11:2).
and sefichei shevi'it. Crops that grew on their own in the Sabbatical year, which the Sages forbade to eat (Hilchot Shemitah 4:2).
liquids that come from their fruits. Juice squeezed from them.
terumot. Chapters 6-10.
and bikkurim. 3:1-6.
and challah. Hilchot Terumot 15:20.
and ma'aser sheni. Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni chapters 2-3.
piggul, nothar and impure. Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 18:6-13.
in the laws of chametz and matzah. Chapters 1-5.
eating on Yom Kippur. Hilchot Shevitat Asor chapter 2.
is not a prohibition of a kind in itself. For the prohibition of eating is on the day, and not on a particular kind of food.
the prohibition of what comes from the vine on the nazirite. For the nazirite is forbidden the various foods produced from the vine; see Hilchot Nezirut 5:1-10.
is not equal for all. For only people who took nazirite vows upon themselves were forbidden it.
wine that was poured as a libation to idolatry. In which a ceremony of pouring was performed as an offering in honor of idolatry.
is forbidden for benefit. Forbidden for benefit, that is, for any use at all.
from what is offered to idolatry. What was offered to idolatry (see also Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:2).
they give him disciplinary lashes. Lashes by rabbinic law.
that a gentile touched. For the manner of touching that forbids see below 12:1.
for the gentile's intention is for idolatry. His intention when he touches wine is for idolatrous worship.
a gentile who touched wine unintentionally. For the details of the law see below 12:5.
one who buys slaves... and circumcised and immersed them. For slaves are immersed for the purpose of slavery (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 13:11).
and idolatry has not ceased from their mouths. They still mention its name.
and minors do not forbid. Who were born into a Jewish environment and do not know idolatrous worship.
as we explained. Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:7.
and one may set aside wine with him. It is permitted to leave wine with him in a special place for a short time.
and one does not deposit wine with him. The reason is explained below 13:12.
any gentile who does not worship idols. And there is no concern that he made a libation of the wine.
but the Christians are idol worshipers. As explained in Hilchot Avodah Zarah 9:4; and see also Hilchot Melachim 11:10-11.
wine that is fit to be offered on the altar. The disqualified wines are detailed in Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 6:9-10.
diluted wine. Mixed with water.
se'or. Leaven.
since it is not fit for the altar. As explained in Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 5:1 (for a similar law see Hilchot Shabbat 29:14).

from when the wine is trodden and begins to flow etc.. From the time the liquid flowing from the trodden grapes begins to flow in the winepress, even before it descends from it into the collection pit.
even if he was bound. Even if the gentile's hands are tied, and there is no worry that he will touch the wine with his hand.
and the skins. The grape skins.
a gentile who trod the wine. In violation (see the previous halacha).
stands over him. Supervises that he not touch.
we do not worry. For this is not the usual way of libation.
a kab or two kabs. A significant amount, which causes the wine in the press to move by the gentile's force.
wineskins. Leather vessels.
and their jars. Wooden or clay vessels.
that he age them. Leave them unused.
until the pitch softens. Melts somewhat.
or until they are heated. If they are not coated with pitch.
three days of twenty-four hours. Three full days.
it is forbidden to drink. For the wine absorbs the taste of the forbidden wine absorbed in the vessel.
brine. The sauce extracted from fish.
muries. Fish fat.
for the salt burns them. The salt in the brine or muries consumes the wine absorbed in the vessel.
and if they were pitched, he rinses them etc.. Coated with pitch; they must be rinsed with water because in the course of pitching it is customary to add a little wine to the pitch.
and he does not bring it in for storage. A vessel used to fill for a short time.
a vessel with which he scoops. With which he draws wine from the barrel or pit.
he rinses it in water and that suffices. For such vessels this kashering is sufficient, and the usual kashering explained above, halacha 15, is not needed.
a clay cup that a gentile drank from. Even if it belongs to an Israelite.
it is forbidden to drink from it the first and second time. The first two times one drinks from it, if he did not rinse it.
drops of wine. Remnant drops of wine.
with lead. Lead.
as potters do. That is how craftsmen make these vessels.
of clay it needs rinsing. A clay cup that is not coated with lead or pitched needs thorough rinsing.
those smoothed with lead. Smoothed with a lead coating.
white or red or black etc.. Types of metal alloys.
if they were white... permitted. With rinsing alone, because the coating prevents the wine from being absorbed in the vessel.
and if they were green they are forbidden. And their law is like ordinary vessels, as explained above, halacha 15.
where he stored it in them for keeping. He put the wine in them to remain there for an extended period.
if he did not store it in them for keeping, he rinses them and they are permitted. As explained above, halacha 17.
rinses them with water and ashes four times. He rinses the winepress with water and rubs ashes over the water, and repeats this a second time.
the winepress shall not be more severe than the jars. Which are made fit by aging or by pouring water, as explained above, halacha 15.
as we explained. In the previous halacha.
strainer. A strainer to filter wine from its dregs.
linen. Flax.
unties them. So that the wine can come out from between the knots.
helef vessels. A kind of plant used to make baskets and the like.
and fibers. Palm fibers.
from wicker baskets. Woven baskets.
the boards. Planks placed on the grapes, on which the beam that presses the grapes is placed.
and the round pieces. Round vessels.
and the poles. Posts to hold the beam with which they press.
the nets. A net that holds the grapes so they do not scatter during pressing.
of planks and of baztzutz. Reeds or hemp.
reed grass. A grass that grows in water.
he scalds them. Soaks them in hot water.
whose waters flow. Washing in a constant, strong stream.
who is presumed to be reliable. Who is known to be careful about the laws of wine kashrut.
and a piece of fish that has no sign. Signs of kashrut.
as we explained. Above 3:21.
even though he does not know him. For an ordinary person is not suspected of giving his guests forbidden things.
on his word. According to the host's statement.
and shakes. Shakes the wine.
an open vessel. But in a sealed vessel the wine is not forbidden (below, halacha 4).
and poured the wine. Poured it into another vessel.
pours. Pours.
for this is not the way of libation. Shaking the vessel as it is carried from place to place is not the way of libation.
holds the mouth of the skin in his hand. And thereby closes the opening of the skin.
permitted, even though the wine sloshes. For this is not the way to pour a libation.
and if it was partly empty, it is permitted. For there is no concern that he touched the wine.
the wine is permitted for benefit only. As mentioned above, 11:5.
the wine came through the force of a gentile etc.. As explained above, halacha 2.
and embraced it. Held the pieces of clay.

permitted for benefit. For although the wine is held by the force of the gentile and is therefore forbidden to drink, this is not a direct action on the wine that forbids benefit (as above, halacha 2), but only an indirect action.
and he grasped the upper crack. In the upper part of the barrel.

the wine is not held by the gentile's strength. The wine is not kept in the barrel because of the gentile's strength, but because the upper part of the barrel presses on the crack, and the gentile merely helps with this.

or if he measured the pit... it is permitted for benefit only. But not for drinking, because in these cases the touching was for a specific purpose, and it is treated as unintentional contact (see above 5:5).
with a reed. A stick used for measuring wine.
slaps the mouth of the boiling barrel. Breaks the bubbles of the wine's fermentation with his hand.
if the gentile climbed out alive, the wine is forbidden for benefit. Even though the fall was unintentional, upon climbing out he might thank an idol for the rescue.
the wine from the top of the barrel to the hole is forbidden. For benefit, since this wine is held directly by the gentile's strength (see above 5:2).
a siphon. A tube made for sucking from.
and sucked the wine. Through the siphon, and this sucking starts the drawing of the wine from the barrel.
the one who pours. Pours out.
the poured stream. The stream of wine while it is being poured.
one who measures for a gentile. Pours a measured quantity of wine into a vessel in the gentile's hand.
let him break it off completely or throw it. He should cut the stream so that there is no connection between the vessels.
a residue of wine. A place where drops of wine remain.
this renders it forbidden. Because the wine in the residue becomes forbidden under the law of a poured stream being a connection, and it forbids the wine that he measures for the Israelite.
nostrils. Openings from which one can drink, like drinking straws.
and he walks after them to watch them. An Israelite walks after the gentiles.
they went a mil away from him. They moved away the distance of a mil.
for he is feared by them. They are afraid the Israelite might see them.
they were out of his sight long enough to open etc.. The gentiles disappeared from the Israelite's view long enough to open the barrel's stopper (the barrel's clay covering) and seal it again.
and it dries. The seal dries.
the wine is permitted. Because the gentile fears that the Israelite might come in and see him touching the wine.
and if he informed him that he was going far away. The Israelite informed the gentile that he was going away for a long time.
in a carriage. In a wagon.
but in open ones. That the gentile can touch immediately.
the dulpeki. A small table from which guests are not accustomed to eat.
what is before him. The wine in the gentile's cup.
in one courtyard. A courtyard shared by several houses.
and both of them left in haste. Unplanned.
and what is from the sides is forbidden. Which he cannot see and is not afraid to touch.
and hid. Concealed himself.
and was caught at it like a thief. Behaved like a thief who was caught.
confident. Calm.
and a child. Whom we do not suspect of touching in order to pour a libation (see further above 11:5).
a troop. An army.
in peacetime. In a time of peace.
he has a loan on that wine. The wine is pledged for a loan that the Israelite owes the gentile.
whose heart is bold with it. He feels that the wine belongs to him.
a gentile prostitute at a banquet of Israelites. At a meal where Jews recline.
if there is moisture of wine there enough to wet the palm etc.. If there is enough moisture in the winepress to wet a palm, so that it would wet another palm.
to rinse... and dry. With water and ashes, as explained above 11:20.
and this is an extra precaution. Since strictly speaking, when there is no moisture, there is no concern of a libation at all.

if it was found opposite a city most of whose people are Israelites, it is permitted etc.. If the barrel was found in a river in the section opposite a certain city, we assume it came from the city, and from the majority group in the city.
for benefit. But not for drinking, since it is not known whether the wine is fit.
if most of the city's thieves are Israelites... it is permitted for drinking. We rely on the majority so as not to forbid the wine.
one who buys a house or rents a house in a gentile's courtyard. He bought or rented a house in a place where his house and the gentile's house open onto the same courtyard.
that the door is open. The door of the house facing the courtyard is open.
and the key and the seal are in his hand. That the house is locked and the wine vessel is sealed.
the gentile might forge. The seal.
that he did not hand over to him the guarding of the house. That handing over the key is not understood as permission to enter the house.
to tread his wine for him in purity. In a way that it will not become forbidden as wine of libation.
and they will take it from him. It will be permitted to buy from him.
if they find out about me, they will not buy from me. At most, they will find out that I forbade the wine and will not buy from me.
the gentile wrote etc.. The gentile wrote in a document that he received money from an Israelite for the wine, although he had not yet actually received it.
it is the gentile's. As long as the Israelite has not actually paid, the gentile considers this wine his own.
as we have explained. In the previous halakhah.
whether in the possession of the wine's owner or in the possession of another gentile. The law is the same in both cases.
the pure. The kosher.
and a garbage heap and a window and a palm tree. Which are opposite the place where the wine is placed, and from which one can see what is done to the wine.
a courtyard divided by a pesifas. A low partition.
roofs. Roofs.
reaches. Arrives.

he need not worry about wine of libation or about ritual purity. There is no need to worry that the gentile went in there and touched the wine, or made objects or foods found there impure, since the domains are separate from one another.
two signs. A double seal that ensures that the vessel remained closed.
this is a seal within a seal. The tight vessel that stops up the barrel is one seal, and the plaster over it is the second seal.
tied. Bound, tied up.
he turned the end of the mouth of the skin inward and tied it. He turned the neck of the leather skin inward and tied it to seal it.
and provided that he designated for him a corner. A specific place in the house for keeping the wine.

cooked wine... and likewise vinegar. In all of these the prohibition of wine of libation does not apply (as explained above 11:9-10), and even if the gentile switches them for others of his own, there will be a prohibition only because of gentiles' ordinary wine (see above 11:3).
and the beer. Which contains a mixture of wine (see Hilchot Nezirut 5:1, according to Orah veSimchah).
and the cheese and the milk. For if the gentile switches them, there will be a prohibition because of the decree against gentiles' milk (above 3:13-15).
wine, meat, and a piece of fish. See above 11:25-26 that one may not buy these, and likewise cheese, except from one presumed to be reliable in kashrut.
that have no sign. Signs of kashrut (and this refers to the fish only, see above 11:25 and the text there).

need two seals. Wine needs two seals to ensure that the gentile did not pour a libation, and meat and fish need them because if the gentile switches them for others, there is a Torah prohibition because of the meat of a carcass or a treifah, or an unclean fish.
because of an aspect of touching. That the prohibition stems from the gentile's touching or the concern about it.
that the gentile was an idol worshiper. Specifically if the gentile was an idol worshiper.
such as an Ishmaelite. Whose ordinary touching forbids only for drinking (above 11:7).
who touched our wine etc.. For in these cases the touch of a gentile who worships idols forbids the wine for drinking only (above 11:5, 12:9).

one who deposits wine etc.. In all these cases the wine is forbidden for drinking when it involves an idol-worshiping gentile (above 12:16; 13:2; 13:9), and the same applies to a resident alien (see also above 11:7).
for all gentiles are equal in it. Including a resident alien.
lest he come to pour the wine. And forbid it, as explained above 12:2.
who empties. Pours out.
and the wine turns out to come from his strength. And it will become forbidden, as explained above 12:2.
that the gentile smells a barrel of our wine. To check the wine's quality and condition.
because it has no substance. A smell has no substance, and this is not a touch.
we have already explained. Above 8:16, Hilchot Ishut 5:2, Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:9.

that its proceeds be forbidden like the proceeds of wine poured as a libation to idolatry. For it was because of this prohibition that they decreed a prohibition on gentiles' ordinary wine (above 11:3).
his wages are forbidden. Because the wages for making the wine count as benefit from the wine.
one who hires a donkey. The gentile hired the donkey from the Israelite.
let him carry them to the Dead Sea. He should throw them into the sea so that they are lost.
so as not to benefit from it. Not to benefit from the ashes of idolatry.
and he placed on it a flask of wine, his wages are permitted. The gentile placed on the donkey the flask of wine he drinks from; it is permitted because he was not hired to transport the wine.
he hired him to break wine of libation. As a laborer who will destroy vessels containing wine of libation.
because he diminishes in prayer. A euphemism for idolatry.
all his wages are forbidden. For the wages were given generally, and his wages include payment also for moving the wine of libation.
and the rest of his wages are permitted. For the wages for each barrel are separate.
that they say to him, give us its value. The value of the barrel, and not the barrel itself.

and if after it came into their possession it is forbidden. If the barrel came into the workers' possession, it became theirs and is forbidden for benefit, and they may not take money in its place, because this money would be considered payment for the wine.
desires its continued existence. Of the wine and the idol, so he actually benefits from them, and not from their value.
to divide. To divide the partnership's property.
so that he not return to his former ways. So that the convert not go back to behaving like a gentile.

and if after they came into the convert's possession it is forbidden. For it is regarded as selling his share of the wine in exchange for the produce (see above 5:20; and see also Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:5).
he set the price before he measured. He fixed the price of the wine before he actually measured the wine into the vessel.

for once he set the price he made up his mind etc.. Once the price is set, the gentile decides in his mind to buy, so by pulling it he acquired the wine, and since he has not yet touched it, it is not wine of libation.
for he has not made up his mind even though he pulled. And in this case pulling does not effect acquisition (Hilchot Mekhirah 4:11).
he must take the money and afterward measure. So that at the time of measuring the wine already belongs to the gentile (see Hilchot Zekhiyah uMattanah 1:14).

for once it touches the vessel it becomes forbidden like gentiles' ordinary wine. From the moment the wine enters the vessel, it is treated as gentiles' wine, even though the acquisition has not yet been completed.
and I will count it for you. Your food against the denar I gave him.
for it is as if he bought him wine of libation and gave it to him to drink. And so the Israelite benefits from wine of libation.
and correspondingly. Similarly.
in the Sabbatical year it is forbidden. When there is concern that they will feed him Sabbatical-year produce, since Sabbatical-year produce may not be fed to a hired worker (Hilchot Shemittah 5:13).
an am ha'aretz. One who is not careful about Sabbatical-year produce and tithes.
and if the worker ate something not tithed. And likewise it is forbidden when there is concern that the shopkeeper will feed the worker something not tithed.
eat and drink with this denar. And he has not yet given the denar to the shopkeeper.
who became obligated. Who committed himself to pay for the eating and drinking.
since his obligation was not specified. Since the householder has not yet given money to the shopkeeper, it is not considered that the workers are eating forbidden food from his money.
distributes his wine to the people etc.. By force, and demands a high payment.

and enter in my place into the king's treasury. You buy in my place the wine the king distributes to the people, and it will be yours and you will pay me for it, and in this way the Israelite is found trading in the king's wine, and this involves benefit from wine of libation.
and rescue me from the treasury. For this is not explicit trading in wine of libation.
by force. Against his will.
it is as if he broke it or burned it, so he must pay. The gentile damaged the wine and must pay as if he had destroyed it with his hands (see Hilchot Chovel uMazik 7:6).
the measure is an average olive's bulk. The amount of food for which one is liable to punishment is the size of an average olive.
and we have already explained. Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:7; and see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1.
and if he ate any amount... they give him lashes for rebellion. Lashes by rabbinic decree (and see also above 3:6).
except what is between the teeth. What is stuck in the teeth is not counted toward the olive's-bulk measure.
what is between the gums. What is on the palate and which he did not swallow.
and he again ate that half-olive's-bulk... he is liable. It is considered that he ate a whole olive's bulk.
or piggul and notar. For eating which one is liable to karet (for their definitions see Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 13:1-3).
and it shrank. It contracted.
