and swelled, one is liable for it to karet or lashes. It swelled, and so returned to the size it originally had.
we have already explained. Above 4:16-17.
and the prohibitions of a nazirite, as will be explained in their place. Hilchot Nezirut chapter 3.
five kinds of grain. The five kinds of grain: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye.
they all combine. See also Hilchot Bikkurim 7:4.
both for the prohibition of chametz on Passover etc.. For all are forbidden to eat at the measure of an olive's bulk (see above 10:23-24).
for anything subject to terumah and tithes. See the rule in Hilchot Terumot 2:1.
combines to an olive's bulk with tevel. To become liable for eating it (see above 10:19).
as we have explained. Above 4:17.
one who eats a large eating. In which there are several olive's-bulk measures.
we do not hold him liable etc.. For similar examples see Hilchot Kilayim 10:30, Hilchot Nezirut 5:10.
like a barley grain or a mustard seed. The size of a barley or mustard seed, which are much smaller than an olive.

if from beginning to end it took the time to eat three eggs' worth. If the time from the start of eating to its end was the time in which one eats bread the size of three eggs (for another example see Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:4).
within the time of eating a peras. The time to eat half a loaf of bread, whose measure is three eggs.
a revi'it. A log.
gentiles' ordinary wine. Wine of gentiles; see its definition above 11:3.
that he dissolved. Softened solid food and turned it into liquid.
the time of drinking a revi'it. For another example see Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:4.
he is not liable for them unless he eats them in a manner of enjoyment. That he eats them in the usual way (see also Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 5:8; and see the supplement: 'Kashrut of medicines').
the prohibition of eating them is stated etc.. The prohibition is written in the Torah not in the language of eating.
in the language of cooking. In the prohibition of meat and milk: "You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk" (Exodus 23:19).
and in the language of sanctification. In the prohibition of kilayim of the vineyard: "lest the fullness be sanctified" (Deuteronomy 22:9).
like one acting unwittingly. Without realizing, with no intention to eat.
if he intended. To benefit from the forbidden thing.
permitted because of danger to life. For saving a life overrides all Torah prohibitions except idolatry, forbidden relations and bloodshed (Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 5:6).
a pregnant woman who smelled etc.. A pregnant woman, where there is danger if she craves a food and does not eat it (see also Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:9).
we feed her from the broth. From the liquid in which the food was cooked, and not from the forbidden item itself.
less than the measure. Pieces smaller than an olive's bulk of the food itself.
for they disturb the soul. They stir up the craving.
until his eyes brighten. Which is a sign that he has recovered.
the lighter, the lighter first. From the lighter prohibition first, as explained in the next halakhah.
the severe. From the severe prohibition.
who was seized by bulmus. A dangerous hunger attacked him (see also Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:9).
we feed him carcass first. For its prohibition is lighter than the prohibition of tevel, and its punishment is lashes (above 4:1).
for tevel is punishable by death. One is liable for eating it to death at the hands of Heaven (above 10:19).
and the aftergrowths of the Sabbatical year. Plants that grew by themselves in the seventh year, which the Sages forbade eating.
as will be explained in Hilchot Shemittah veYovel. Shemittah 4:2.
and Sabbatical-year produce. Sabbatical-year produce after its time of removal, which is forbidden to eat under a positive commandment (ibid. 7:1-3).
to rectify the tevel. To separate terumah and tithes from it.
we have already explained. Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8.
come at once. That two prohibitions took effect at the same time (for examples see above 2:1, 5:5, Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 11:9).
an additional prohibition. That the added prohibition has an extra stringency beyond the first prohibition (for examples see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:8, Hilchot Terumot 10:25).
an inclusive prohibition. That the prohibition applies to other things that are permitted, which include the forbidden item (for examples see above 7:2, 8:6).
as one who eats suet. Above 7:1.
as one who eats notar. Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 13:3.
and as one who eats on Yom Kippur. Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:1-2.
and as an impure person who ate sacred food. Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 18:13.
and as one who benefited from sacred property and committed me'ilah. Hilchot Me'ilah 3:1.
and since the prohibition of benefit was added to it. An 'additional prohibition'.
the prohibition of sacred offerings applied to it as well. The prohibition of sacrifices can take effect on it.
permitted to the Most High. It can be offered on the altar.
notar. That the permitted time for eating it has passed.
since a prohibition for the Most High was added to it. An 'additional prohibition'.
became forbidden to a layman. The prohibition of notar applied to it.
and this eater. The person eating, when he was pure.
became impure, it became forbidden even its meat. If he became impure it is forbidden to eat sacred meat, including the fat, and this is an 'inclusive prohibition'.
it included all foods. For everything is forbidden to eat on Yom Kippur.

and since it became forbidden even among unconsecrated food, its prohibition was added to this fat. Because it is an 'inclusive prohibition', the additional prohibition of eating on Yom Kippur applies to it.
a kind with a kind not its own. A mixture of two different kinds (for a fuller definition of what counts as a kind with its own kind see below 16:14-15).
by imparting taste. If the forbidden item does not impart taste to the permitted item, the mixture is permitted.
for its taste cannot be determined. It is impossible to identify the taste of the forbidden item.
it is nullified by a majority. And if most of the mixture is permitted, the entire mixture is permitted.
kidney fat. The layer of fat surrounding the kidneys, which is forbidden to eat (above 7:5).
its substance. Substance of the fat, as explained in the next halakhah.

an olive's bulk in every three eggs. That the amount of fat in the mixture is in the proportion of an olive's bulk of fat to every three eggs' worth of the mixture (and this is also the measure of time within which the prohibition combines to make one liable for eating, above 14:8; and see Hilchot Chametz uMatzah 1:6).
lashes for rebellion by their decree. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
to the fat of the tail. And the fat of the tail is permitted to eat (above 7:5).
kidney fat fell into the fat of the tail. And this is a mixture of a kind with its own kind, which is nullified by a majority (above 5:1).
like two. Twice, and not necessarily double, but a majority suffices (Me'iri).
because of its tiny quantity. Because of its minuscule amount.
whose appearance stands out. It is noticeable in its appearance and can be distinguished.
as will be explained. Below chapter 16.
in the measure that the Sages gave etc.. And it will be explained below in halakhah 13 and on.
of wine of libation. Wine that was poured as a libation to idolatry (see its definition above 11:1).
of tevel. Grain from which terumah and tithes have not been separated.
for it can be rectified. Terumah and tithes can be separated from it even after it became mixed.
as will be explained. Below 16:28.
as will be explained in its place. Hilchot Ma'aser 8:2.
Sabbatical-year produce. Produce that grew in the Sabbatical year, to which sanctity applies and which must be eaten under certain restrictions.

even though if they became mixed with their own kind, in any amount etc.. The measure of nullification of Sabbatical-year produce in a mixture differs from the rules of nullification stated here, which forbid with its own kind in any amount and not in sixty (Hilchot Shemittah 7:22).

they are not among the Torah prohibitions, that this mixture is not forbidden etc.. The difference stems from the fact that this is not a prohibition of eating, but an obligation to eat it in sanctity.
as will be explained in its place. There 5:1.
as we have explained. Hilchot Chametz uMatzah 1:5.
to new grain. Grain of this year, which is forbidden to eat before the omer offering is brought (for details of the law see above 10:2-5).
with old. Grain from the previous year.
it has permitters. There is a way by which the new grain will become permitted.
muktzeh. Foods that were not designated for eating from the eve of the festival, and which are forbidden to eat on the festival (Hilchot Yom Tov 1:17-18).
and nolad. Such as an egg laid on a festival, which is forbidden to eat on the festival (see ibid. 1:19-20).
for it has a way by which it will be permitted. For muktzeh and nolad are permitted to eat after the festival.

such as hekdesh and second tithe. Hekdesh is permitted after redemption (Hilchot Arachin vaCharamim 7:1), and second tithe that became mixed in Jerusalem has a permitted way by eating the mixture in Jerusalem, and if it became mixed outside Jerusalem, it can be redeemed or brought to Jerusalem and eaten there (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 6:14).
and the like. For more examples see Hilchot Yom Tov 1:20, Hilchot Nedarim 5:12, Hilchot Bikkurim 4:15.
orlah. The fruit of a tree in the first three years after its planting (above 10:9).
and kilayim of the vineyard. Grain or vegetables that grew together with the vine (above 10:6).
which have no way of permission for everyone. Terumah is permitted to a priest but not to a layman, and therefore it is not defined as something that has permitters.
by imparting taste, as we have explained. Above 5:6.
and do not be surprised about chametz on Passover. That even if it is mixed with something not its own kind, its mixture is forbidden in any amount.

for the Torah forbade any leavening agent. The Sages explained that a leavening agent is a mixture containing chametz (see Hilchot Chametz uMatzah 1:6), and they derived from this verse that there is a prohibition in all other mixtures of forbidden items. And because the prohibition of mixtures in other prohibitions is learned from chametz, they were stricter with its mixture than with the mixture of other prohibitions.
as we have explained. Above 5:9.
the measures that the Sages gave. That something is nullified by virtue of its small quantity (see above halakhot 4-5).
terumah... and bikkurim. That became mixed with unconsecrated grain.
rise in one hundred and one. They are nullified in a mixture at this ratio (see also Hilchot Terumot 13:1, 15:21).
and he must lift out. Separate from the mixture the measure of priestly gifts that belongs to the priests (see below halakhah 15).

and they combine with one another. Even though these are different kinds of prohibition, such as a mixture of terumah and challah that fell into unconsecrated food, they combine together to render the mixture forbidden.

the showbread. The bread placed on the table in the Temple (Hilchot Temidin uMusafin 5:1). And only showbread that became impure is nullified at one hundred, but pure showbread that became mixed with unconsecrated food is not nullified at one hundred (see Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 6:23-24).
one se'ah against the se'ah that fell. For in the mixture there is certainly one se'ah of priestly gifts that belongs to the priests (see below halakhah 15).
meduma. A mixture of unconsecrated food and terumah (for details of its law see Hilchot Terumot chapters 13-15).
orlah and kilayim of the vineyard. And these are forbidden for benefit (above 10:9).
and he need not lift out. The portion of the forbidden item found in the mixture.
the money of priests. And it is forbidden to rob what belongs to them.
that priests are not particular about it. About losing such trivial terumot, whose value is very low (see also Hilchot Terumot 13:1; for another example see ibid. 3:3).
poor figs. Inferior figs.
are forbidden for benefit. And not only for eating, therefore the Sages were strict to forbid the mixture at a double ratio.
terumat ma'aser. The tenth that a Levite separates from the tithe he received and gives to a priest.
and renders forbidden. Forbids.
all the other Torah prohibitions. That became mixed with something permitted, of its own kind.
the size of a barley grain of fat. Fat in the amount of a barley grain.
as we have explained. Above 8:1.
since the gid hanasheh is a creature in itself. And a complete creature is more stringent than other things that become mixed (see also above 8:2).

and the gid itself is not measured and does not forbid etc.. The gid hanasheh itself is not counted in the measure of sixty for permitting, and it also does not combine with the fat to forbid, because it has no taste (see also below 16:6).
a udder. The animal's udder.
in sixty. And the udder itself is forbidden to eat (above 9:13).
and the udder counts toward the number. The udder is included in the measure of sixty although it is itself forbidden.
as we have explained. Above 9:12-13.
an egg in which a chick was found. Which began to form in it, and this egg is forbidden to eat (above 3:8).
that was cooked with permitted eggs. And as a result of the cooking, taste from the chick was released into the other eggs.
because it is a creature in itself etc.. And the Sages were stringent in this case.
did not forbid them. For the taste of eggs does not forbid, as it is like water.
beat these with those. Broke the eggs and mixed them together.
or if the egg of an impure bird became mixed etc.. So that it is impossible to distinguish and remove the forbidden egg.

for the portion raised from the nazirite's ram, namely the foreleg etc.. The foreleg that is raised from the nazirite's ram and given to the priest is permitted to eat only for priests (see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 9:9-12), and it does not forbid the rest of the sacrificial meat to the owners to eat, even though it is cooked with it.
we view the fat of the tail and the groats as if they were one body. Even though they are not one kind, they combine into the permitted portion of the mixture that nullifies the kidney fat.

it is impossible here to determine the taste. It is impossible to identify the taste of the forbidden item because the taste of the fat of the tail and of the kidney fat is identical, and so we measure by sixty, as for a kind with its own kind.
and the same applies to terumot etc.. When a kind with its own kind and something else became mixed.
and in what the pot absorbed after the forbidden item fell. The food absorbed in the walls of the pot during cooking from the moment the forbidden item fell into it.
by estimation of judgment. Approximately.
exactly. Precisely.
to nullify Torah prohibitions in the first place. To cause a prohibition to be nullified in a mixture (for further examples see below 16:12, Hilchot Terumot 13:10).
so that it rises. So that the prohibition is nullified and the mixture becomes permitted to eat.
everything is permitted. To others.
milk that fell into a pot containing poultry meat. Whose mixture is forbidden by rabbinic decree (above 9:4).
we have already explained. Above 5:1.
if the forbidden item spoiled the permitted one and ruined its taste. The taste of the forbidden item spoiled the taste of the permitted item.
the priest. One permitted to eat terumah.
meduma. A forbidden mixture of unconsecrated food and terumah.
and the law of meduma will be explained in Hilchot Terumot. Hilchot Terumot chapters 13-15.
as we have explained. Above halakhah 28.
that he roasted it in its fat. Without removing the forbidden fat.
kidney fat... fat of the entrails. Fats that are forbidden to eat (above 7:5).
peels and eats until he reaches the fat. Since the kid is lean, its fat does not impart taste and does not forbid its meat for eating.
peels and eats. Although the gid itself is forbidden to eat (above 8:1), since it does not impart taste, it does not forbid the thigh.
and did not remove from it either the threads or the forbidden membranes. Which are forbidden because of blood or fat (see above 7:10).
that smelled. The smell of the foods that spreads in the space of the oven.
the substance of the forbidden item itself. Substance of the forbidden item.
salted carcass meat. That has salt on it.
that the essence of the carcass is absorbed into the body of the properly slaughtered animal's meat. For the power of salt causes carcass meat to release forbidden matter (see above 9:18).
unsalted. That is not salted.
because of its brine. For the kosher fish absorbs from the fatty brine released from the unclean fish because of the salting.
for the unsalted absorbs from the salted. And the salted does not absorb from the unsalted.
that he pickled it. In salt or vinegar or something else.
leavens. Causes a leavening reaction.
leavens or seasons etc.. See also Hilchot Terumot 15:4.
or something important when it stands as it is etc.. That those things stand on their own and are not mixed with the permitted food.
meduma. A mixture of unconsecrated food and terumah (for details of its law see Hilchot Terumot chapters 13-15).
sourdough of kilayim of the vineyard. A leavening agent made from grain that grew together with a vine.
everything is forbidden for benefit. As is the law of kilayim of the vineyard and orlah (see above 10:6, 10:9).
Perach... Badan. Names of places.
sealed. Closed.
and spinach shoots. Spinach leaves that grow from the spinach roots after it was cut.
and large cabbage heads. Large cabbages.
and a householder's loaves. Bread baked at home and not in a bakery.
he serves it honorably before the guests. He presents it as an honored dish to guests.
until he lifts out that piece and then estimates the rest in sixty. He removes the forbidden piece, and estimates whether the rest contains sixty times the taste released from the piece.

and the same applies to a piece of meat in milk. Which is forbidden for benefit by the Torah (see above 9:1), and although its prohibition does not stem from the piece itself but from the milk absorbed in it, it forbids in any amount.
unconsecrated animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard. An unconsecrated animal slaughtered in the courtyard of the Temple, which is forbidden for benefit by rabbinic decree.
as will be explained in Hilchot Shechitah. 2:2-3.
for the sinews do not impart taste. Because it lacks taste, the sinew itself has no power to forbid (see the rule above 15:17).
because it is a creature in itself. See also above 15:17.
the ox that is stoned etc.. All of these are forbidden for benefit, and therefore they forbid the whole mixture for benefit.
even though they are usually counted. And they have some importance, they nevertheless are nullified in their measure.
that they are usually counted. To be counted individually.
everything is permitted. For they are nullified at two hundred (above 15:14).
for all these prohibitions. Listed above, which forbid their mixture in any amount.
one pomegranate fell from this mixture. Of the pomegranate of Badan, a forbidden item mixed with permitted pomegranates (above halakhah 4).

nullification by majority is stated only to permit a doubt of a doubt. For in the first mixture there is certainly a forbidden item, in the second mixture there is a doubtful prohibition, and in the third mixture a double doubt, and in this case even something that forbids in any amount is nullified.
nuts were cracked etc.. In the cases detailed below the important item is not whole, and so it loses its importance and does not forbid in any amount (and see also Hilchot Terumot 15:1).
that was pounded. Crushed or cut into small pieces.
and everything became like it. All the pieces were crushed and the carcass piece is not recognizable among them.
as we have explained. Above 15:25.
forbidden to an Israelite. For both kilayim of the vineyard and terumah are forbidden to an Israelite.

and permitted to priests. Because terumah is permitted to priests, and kilayim of the vineyard, although forbidden even to a priest, does not have enough leavening in itself; and since the prohibition is caused by the combination of terumah and kilayim of the vineyard, it is a case of 'this and that cause', and it is permitted (see below halakhah 24).
names of one kind. Equal kinds with different names.
kinds with one name. Different kinds with a similar name.
river karpas etc.. Kinds of karpas named for the place they grow.
afar. Meadow grass.

if there is enough in the sourdough to leaven... everything is forbidden. By the law that something that leavens or seasons forbids in any amount (above halakhah 1), even though in practice they did not leaven or season.

terumah raises etc.. Even though it is itself forbidden to an Israelite and is not nullified, since there are not a hundred against it, it combines with the permitted portion in the mixture to nullify orlah or kilayim of the vineyard, and the mixture is permitted to priests to eat.
that fell into twenty thousand of unconsecrated food. And their prohibition was nullified in the mixture.

and even though part of the hundred... orlah or kilayim of the vineyard. Since their prohibition was nullified at first, they became like unconsecrated food and combine with the rest of the permitted portion to nullify the terumah.
with orlah peels. Dye produced from the peels of orlah fruit.
it must be burned. For it is forbidden to benefit even from the peels of orlah fruit (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni veNeta Revai 9:12).

for its benefit is recognizable in them. Even though they contain no substance of the forbidden item, their existence came from the forbidden item and this is noticeable in them, therefore they are forbidden for benefit.
became mixed with others. The dish or the bread.
a sit's worth that was dyed with orlah. A thread two fingers long that was dyed with orlah (see Hilchot Shabbat 9:7, Commentary on the Mishnah Orlah 3:2, Hilchot Shabbat 13:4).
orlah dyes. Dye produced from orlah fruit.
dye water. Water mixed with dye produced from orlah fruit.
is nullified by a majority. For here there is not the substance of the forbidden item but only its appearance.
let it cool. Let him wait for it to cool.
let him heat it. They should fire it.

that the improvement of forbidden wood is in the bread or in the dish. The forbidden wood benefited the dish and forbade it (for other examples see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:13, Hilchot Chametz uMatzah 3:11).
for the forbidden wood is gone. For since the source of the heat and its main part has departed, this is not real benefit from the forbidden item.
the potter. The pot maker.
for something forbidden for benefit etc.. For the clay vessels were made with the help of orlah peels.
a pot in which he cooked it. In which he cooked a dish.
with orlah peels or with kilayim of the vineyard and with permitted wood. One after the other.

and even though this and that cause etc.. Although generally when a forbidden item and a permitted item together cause a result, it is permitted (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:14, Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni veNeta Revai 10:21), that is only when they caused it at once, but one after the other it is forbidden.
that became mixed with saplings. So that the orlah sapling is not recognizable among the saplings.

and by law they should forbid everything to him. Out of concern that he would come to mix an orlah sapling deliberately among permitted saplings in order to nullify it, and one may not nullify a prohibition in the first place (see above 15:25).
for it is a presumption. The assumption is.
that a person does not forbid his vineyard with a single sapling. And he will not come to plant orlah in it in the first place in order to nullify it.
one who curdles. Makes cheese.
with the sap of unripe orlah fruit. Sap that comes out of unripe orlah fruit.
with the rennet of an idolatrous offering. The stomach lining of an animal that was offered to an idol, and one curdles cheese with its hide.

even though it is a kind with a kind not its own. Although above 5:1 it was explained that a leavening agent, seasoning and something important forbid in any amount only with their own kind, while a kind with a kind not its own is by imparting taste, the law differs for a curdling agent, which forbids in any amount even with a kind not its own, since it causes the thing to come into being.
for the forbidden thing etc.. See above 3:13.
and their liquids shall be buried. See also Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 19:10.
as we have said. Above 15:6-7.
from a small flask. A small vessel.
each first one is nullified. Each drop that streams into the wine pit is nullified the moment it mixes with the permitted wine (for another example see Hilchot Tumat Met 2:14).
he poured from the barrel etc.. Because the stream is large and is poured out all at once, it cannot be said that 'each first one is nullified'.
for the descending stream. The flow.
gentiles' ordinary wine. Wine of gentiles about which it is not known whether it was poured as a libation to idolatry and which is forbidden for benefit (above 11:3).
it forbids in any amount for drinking. Like wine of libation, which forbids in any amount, but they permitted him to benefit from it.
and throws it into the Dead Sea. Throws the coins into the sea so that they are lost.
in water. The forbidden.
provided it is poured from a small flask. See above halakhah 28.
such as those that were worshiped. That people bowed down to them as idolatry (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 8:2).
an idolatrous offering. That were offered before an idol (ibid. 7:2).
a large jug. A large vessel.

we view the permitted wine as if it were not there. Although above 15:22 it was explained that when a kind with its own kind and something else became mixed, the thing that is its own kind combines with the thing not its own kind and the prohibition is nullified, this applies only to prohibitions nullified with their own kind at sixty and with a kind not their own by imparting taste. But since wine of libation forbids with its own kind in any amount (above 15:6), the permitted wine has no power to combine with the water and nullify it.
if they are fit to nullify the taste of that wine of libation. By the law of a kind with a kind not its own, which is nullified when it does not impart taste.
let him rinse them. Rinse with water.
split. Cracked.

whether it was new. Although new wine is similar in taste to grapes, there is still a difference between them, and it is considered a kind with a kind not its own, whose measure is by imparting taste.
for the wine spoils the taste of the figs. And something that imparts a spoiled taste is permitted (above 15:28).
he will sell them again to an Israelite. And the Israelite will stumble by eating a forbidden item.
not in the presence of an Israelite. Not in the presence of another Israelite, so that he not buy this bread from the gentile.
as will be explained. Below 17:9.
and why do we not check the wheat by imparting taste. By the law of a kind with a kind not its own.
we measure it by imparting taste. By the law of a kind with a kind not its own.

he cooked in it a kind of meat, the dish is forbidden. When there is not sixty in the dish against the forbidden item absorbed in the pot, but when there is sixty, the dish is permitted by the law of a kind with its own kind (above 15:6).
he cooked in it another kind, by imparting taste. By the law of a kind with a kind not its own, which forbids by imparting taste (for another example see above 9:11).
of that day. In which a forbidden item was cooked that same day.
since the fat has not yet spoiled. For after the fat has spoiled, it imparts a spoiled taste to the dish and does not forbid it (above 15:28).
coated with lead. Smoothed with a lead coating.
that were used with hot liquids. In which hot food was placed that was absorbed in the walls of the pot.
from the second day onward. From taking them from the gentile.
the dish is permitted. After the fact, because the pot is not of that day.
and jugs. Drinking vessels.
rinses them. Washes the dirt with water.
by means of hot liquids. In water or a dish that was boiled on a fire.
pots. Cooking pots.
and kettles. Kettles.
and water heaters. Vessels in which water or a dish is heated.
by means of fire. Direct use on the fire, such as roasting and the like.
and grills. Metal grates on which meat is roasted.
until their surface peels off. Until the outer layer of these vessels falls off.
a small pot. The pot that has forbidden matter absorbed in it.
and if it was a large pot. That cannot fit inside another pot (see also Hilchot Chametz uMatzah 5:26).
he surrounds its rim with dough or clay. He creates an extension of the pot's walls so that the boiling water reaches its rim as well.
as we have explained. Above halakhah 2.
in which. In vessels that are not of that day.
is not for the matter of impurity and purity. Its reason is not impurity and purity like other immersions.
and from oral tradition. Tradition.
in its purification from the cooked food of gentiles. In the process of purification after taking a vessel from a gentile.
for you have no impurity that is not removed except by fire. There is no impurity whose purification depends on passing through fire.

and the impurity of the dead by sprinkling and immersion. One impure through contact with the dead is sprinkled with the water of the red heifer, immerses, and becomes pure at nightfall (see the rule in Hilchot Parah 11:1).
and there is no fire at all except for the matter of the cooked food of gentiles. The role of the fire is to release the absorbed forbidden matter from the gentiles' cooked food.
he added purity to it. By immersing it in water.
to permit it from the cooked food of gentiles. To complete the process of its purification from gentiles' cooked food.
those taken from gentiles. That were bought from them.
metal vessels. And likewise glass vessels (above halakhah 3) because they resemble metal, since they can be repaired by melting.
rinses or boils or heats to glowing. To remove the absorbed forbidden matter from the vessels (as above halakhah 3).
wooden vessels or stone vessels. These vessels do not require immersion because the verse from which the obligation of immersion was learned mentions only metal vessels.
new earthenware vessels. That gentiles have not used.
that was good. Without defects.
and he wants to eat hot food in it. Because heat causes absorption and release, sticking it in the ground is not enough.
or to slaughter with it. Because the knife is pressed during slaughter and releases the forbidden matter from itself into the meat, sticking it in the ground is not enough.
peeled. The place of slaughter.
on its whetstone. A wheel for sharpening knives.
in hard ground. Uncultivated ground.
until he rinses it, even in cold water. Because the place of slaughter is cold, but if he wants to use it with hot food, it needs to be stuck in the ground (see above 6:20).
to intermarriage. To marry gentiles.
their bread or their cooked food. Bread they baked and food they cooked.
to their forbidden foods. To eating forbidden foods.
cooked wine, which is not forbidden. See above 11:9.
or that the drinker be from his own vessels alone. That he drinks his own wine from his own vessels.
and one does not drink beer. Even though it is not included in wine (see above 11:10).
it is like wine and is poured as a libation. It is poured on the altar, and therefore it is fit to be considered wine (see the rule above 11:9).
the baker. The one who bakes.
and in the field. A distant place with no bakeries.
householders' bread. Baked in a gentile's home.
he lowered the fire. Reduced the intensity of the fire.
perishin. Quinces (and in some places there is a kind of quince eaten raw, R. Y. Kafih).
that is eaten as it is raw. Eaten even without cooking.
and unsalted fish. That is not salted.
and vegetables. That are not eaten raw.
and the Israelite did not take part with him. See below halakhah 16.
goes up on the tables of kings. Food served before important people.
lupine seeds. Lupine beans.
that were boiled. That they boiled in water.

permitted. Since salting is considered the beginning of cooking, the gentile's roasting afterward does not forbid. And even if the gentile salted at the start, the gentile's salting is not considered cooking that forbids (below halakhah 17).
and stirred the pot. Mixed the dish.
and fruits that he smoked. To give the fruits a smoky taste.

salted is not like boiling for this decree. For the matter of gentiles' cooking, they did not treat salting as an act resembling boiling that forbids as cooking (see above 9:18 regarding meat and milk).
roasted grains. Roasted legumes or grain kernels.
that are boiled. Cooked in water without spices.
as a side dish. As an addition to the main food.
and because of the cooked food of gentiles everywhere. Even in a place where they do not go up on the tables of kings, they are forbidden because of forbidden foods.
sufganin. Doughnuts.
are forbidden even because of the cooked food of gentiles. In addition to the prohibition because of gentiles' cooking, because they absorb forbidden matter from the vessels in which they are fried.
in the marsh. In the meadow.
singed the head. Of an animal.
from the dildulin. Small pieces of meat hanging from the animal's head.
permitted. For they could be eaten even without cooking.
average. That can be eaten with difficulty.
roasted lentil flour. Flour produced from roasted lentils.
this is forbidden. When kneading them in vinegar is forbidden because of gentiles' vinegar (above 11:13), they forbade even when he kneaded them with water.
roasted flour of wheat and barley. Flour produced from roasted wheat or barley.
this is permitted. Since people are accustomed to knead them with water, they did not forbid them.
who rebelled against the court's ruling that permitted it. Who rebelled against the decision of Rabbi and his court, who permitted gentiles' oil (Mishnah Avodah Zarah 2:6).
even though they cooked the oil. In a gentile's vessel.
for the meat spoils the oil. Even though the oil was cooked in a vessel in which meat had been cooked earlier, the oil did not become forbidden because the taste of the meat was spoiled.
gentiles' kuspan. Oil produced by heating or pouring hot water over the waste of fruit or grain, such as dates or sesame.
permitted. Both with regard to gentiles' cooking and with regard to gentiles' absorbed forbidden matter.
pickled things. Vegetables pickled in liquid, and they are permitted because pickling is not considered cooking.
forbidden. Out of concern for wine of libation.
what is taken from the storehouse is permitted. For the placing of the wine lees is done close to its sale and not while it is in the storehouse.
the muryas. Fish oil.
and by this they instruct. According to this principle.
the court is not commanded to separate him from it. See also Hilchot Evel 3:12, Hilchot Yibbum vaChalitzah 7:18, Hilchot Shabbat 24:11.
to separate him. To prevent him from committing the prohibited act.
shevut. Whose prohibition is by rabbinic decree (Hilchot Shabbat 21:1).
is dulled from them. Is pushed away from them.
mourns. Is distressed.
barbers. Bloodletters.
who draw blood from them. Who remove blood.
lashes for rebellion. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
that he delay his excretions. Hold back from relieving himself.
in addition to. On top of.
to accustom himself to set times. To set fixed times for relieving himself (see also Hilchot De'ot 5:6).
so that he not have to go far in front of people. For if he needs to relieve himself in a place where people are present, he will have to go far or delay, and will come to revulsion.
